feed.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack

entry.title: Handling PQ signatures on the stack
entry.summary:
Opcode blacklisting can undermine the flexibility of stack manipulation, especially when handling large signature data on the regular stack. While certain operations, such as using OP_SIZE on SHRINCS signatures, still permit the restriction of signatures to stateful or stateless paths, this approach restricts duplication and other creative script constructions that could otherwise leverage signature data in versatile ways.
In contrast, maintaining an isolated signature stack offers a more straightforward solution if advanced script interactions with signature data are not a priority or are postponed until features like GSR or similar technologies are adopted separately. An isolated stack brings the additional advantage of potentially qualifying for a greater witness data discount, as outlined in [this discussion](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/segwit-commitment-to-post-quantum-witness-data/2702). The expectation had been that new witness discounts would not coincide with the rollout of SHRINCS. However, if simultaneous deployment is under consideration, a more comprehensive approach should be explored.
A potential direction involves adopting witness style variations, akin to the proposals described by @sipa—further detailed [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/segwit-commitment-to-post-quantum-witness-data/2702/17)—which could provide greater flexibility and efficiency in witness data management while enabling future extensibility for script innovation.
